placements.why: This envelope's whole content is an instrument-calibration report (Kestrelwood spectrograph, verified against dated reference plates, holding across the observing band). Nothing in the existing (empty) strata or graph structure covers organizational tracking of calibration events, but 'Calibration' is itself named in the org's own strata vocabulary (Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration) — this is the first envelope to actually instantiate it, an exact fit rather than an invented category.
placements.title: Calibration as an organizational category
placements.frame: What has been calibrated, against what reference standard, and does the result hold across the full range it is meant to cover?

placements.title: Calibration is verified against a dated reference standard and confirmed to hold across the instrument's full range
placements.frame: Has this instrument's calibration been checked against a specific, dated reference standard, and does it hold across the full range it is meant to serve — or only under narrow conditions?
placements.why: src-1 narrates the core claim — the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration verified against the June reference plates and holding across the full observing band — a subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets, other bands) will keep feeding, satisfying the narrative grain test. src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument-and-calibration facts as structured fields rather than prose; per the fact rule they join this leaf's support as evidence rather than minting their own leaf, since their content is the same verification-against-standard theme in catalogue form (also reflected in the position pass's StructuredCalibrationFields grouping of exactly these two).
